mainTopic: Sins and their punishments: the ברייתא from גזל through גלות and נבלות פה, הדרוקן as a sign of sin, and the four signs
overview: This amud continues a long ברייתא that matches sins with the national punishments they bring, and it proves each punishment from פסוקים. It opens with the last proofs for גזל: locusts, famine, and, through an אל תקרי reading, people eating their own children. Corrupt judging and ביטול תורה bring sword, plague, and famine. False and empty oaths, חילול השם, and חילול שבת bring wild beasts and empty roads, and a גזירה שוה on the word חילול links them together. שפיכות דמים destroys the בית המקדש and drives away the שכינה. גילוי עריות, עבודה זרה, and neglecting שמיטה and יובל bring גלות. נבלות פה brings harsh troubles, and the אמוראים add that it reverses good decrees and deepens גיהנם, even for a silent listener. The גמרא then discusses הדרוקן as a sign of sin, shows that it has other causes too, and tells how שמואל הקטן, אביי, and רבא got it without sinning. The amud ends with four signs of four sins and the opening of a new ברייתא about אסכרה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proofs that theft brings blight and locusts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining the 'cows of Bashan' (women who eat without working and push their husbands to steal). It then brings פסוקים showing that theft brings שדפון, ירקון, and swarms of locusts.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the women who eat and do not work. And it is written: 'I struck you with blight and mildew; the locust devoured your many gardens, vineyards, fig trees, and olive trees.' And it is written: 'What the גזם left, the ארבה ate; what the ארבה left, the ילק ate; what the ילק left, the חסיל ate.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of proving the punishments for גזל. The גמרא brings פסוקים showing that blight and locusts come because of theft.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, the ברייתא said that theft brings locusts (גובאי), famine, and people eating the flesh of their own sons and daughters. The 'cows of Bashan' פסוק showed that theft was the sin being punished. The פסוקים in עמוס and יואל now prove the locust punishment: crops eaten by wave after wave of locusts. The blight in עמוס is part of the same פסוק and is not a separate item in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Theft or robbery, the sin being discussed here
Blight, a crop disease caused by scorching wind
Mildew, a disease that turns crops yellow
Different kinds or stages of locusts

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. 'Who eat and do not work' describes the 'cows of Bashan' from the end of the previous daf. These are women who demand luxuries without working, which pushes their husbands to steal.

phrases.english: who eat and do not work.
phrases.notes: Explains the 'cows of Bashan' from the previous daf.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'I struck you with blight and mildew;'
the multitude of your gardens and your vineyards,
your fig trees and your olive trees, the gazam-locust devoured.'
And it is written: 'What the gazam left, the arbeh ate;'
and what the arbeh left, the yelek ate;
and what the yelek left, the chasil ate.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof for גזל that began on the previous daf.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that theft brings locusts (גובאי)

steps.title: Hunger without being full, and eating one's own children
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in ישעיה shows that people grab food and stay hungry. An אל תקרי reading turns 'the flesh of his arm' into 'the flesh of his offspring', describing terrible famine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'He snatches on the right and is hungry, he eats on the left and is not satisfied; each man eats the flesh of his arm.' Do not read 'the flesh of his arm' (זרועו); rather, read 'the flesh of his offspring' (זרעו).
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last proof for the theft section. It shows famine, and through an אל תקרי reading it proves that people will eat their own children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that because of theft there is famine, and people eat the flesh of their own sons and daughters. ישעיה's picture of grabbing right and left and staying hungry proves the famine. The אל תקרי reading, 'the flesh of his offspring' (זרעו), is the proof for the most terrible part of the punishment: people eating their own children.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not read' — a דרשה technique that rereads a word with slightly different vowels or letters

steps.whatToRemember: The punishments for גזל are locusts, famine, and people eating the flesh of their own children. Each one is proven from a פסוק, the last through an אל תקרי reading.
steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not mean the פסוק's text is changed. It adds an extra layer of meaning on top of the plain reading.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'He snatches on the right and is hungry,'
and he eats on the left and they are not satisfied;
each man eats the flesh of his own arm.'
Do not read 'the flesh of his arm,'
but rather 'the flesh of his offspring.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final proof for the theft punishments.
steps.raayaObject: Theft brings famine, and people eat the flesh of their own children
steps.raayaSupportSource: Isaiah 9:19, read with an אל תקרי

steps.title: Corrupt justice and neglect of Torah bring sword, plague, and famine
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא opens a new section. Four sins (delaying, twisting, and spoiling justice, and ביטול תורה) bring war, looting, plague, drought, and rationed bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the sin of delaying justice, perverting justice, ruining justice, and neglecting Torah: sword and looting increase, plague and drought come, people eat and are not full, and they eat their bread by weight.
steps.whatsHappening: A new sin-and-punishment pair begins. First the ברייתא states the rule; the proofs come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three justice sins cover different failures. עינוי הדין is a judge delaying a ruling, עיוות הדין is deliberately twisting it, and קלקול הדין is ruining it through carelessness. ביטול תורה is grouped with them, and the punishments are war, disease, and scarce food.

keyTerms.meaning: Delaying justice — a judge putting off a ruling

phrases.english: Because of the sin of delaying justice, and perverting justice,
and ruining justice, and neglecting Torah —
sword and looting increase,
and plague and drought come,
and people eat and are not satisfied,
and they eat their bread by weight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from גזל to a new list of sins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Corrupt justice and ביטול תורה bring sword, looting, plague, drought, and rationed bread that does not satisfy.

steps.title: The sword comes for breaking the covenant, and the covenant is Torah
steps.stepSummary: The 'avenging sword' in ויקרא is for breaking the ברית. A פסוק in ירמיה shows that ברית means Torah, which is studied day and night.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'I will bring upon you a sword that avenges the vengeance of the covenant...' And 'covenant' means nothing other than Torah, as it says: 'If not for My covenant day and night...'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins proving the punishments, starting with the sword. It ties the sword directly to neglecting Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the sword avenges the ברית, but it does not say which sin that is. The ירמיה פסוק describes a ברית kept 'day and night', and only Torah study fits that description. So the sword is the punishment for ביטול תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Covenant — here explained as meaning Torah

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And I will bring a sword upon you'
that avenges the vengeance of the covenant, etc.'
And 'covenant' means nothing other than Torah,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אִם לֹא בְרִיתִי יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: as it is said: 'If not for My covenant day and night, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְהֵבֵאתִי עֲלֵיכֶם חֶרֶב נוֹקֶמֶת נְקַם בְּרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins proving the rule from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Sword and plague come because of ביטול תורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: Leviticus 26:25, with ברית explained by Jeremiah 33:25

steps.title: Bread by weight, and the link to rejecting justice
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק describes broken bread supplies and bread handed out by weight. Another פסוק ties these curses to rejecting God's משפטים, which is the corrupt-justice part of the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'When I break your staff of bread, ten women will bake...' And it is written: 'Because, and precisely because, they rejected My judgments.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes this section's proofs. It shows the famine punishment and connects it to perverting justice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'staff of bread' פסוק goes on to say bread will be returned 'by weight' and people will not be satisfied, matching the ברייתא's words. 'They rejected My judgments' links the whole set of curses to the justice sins, not only to ביטול תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Staff of bread' — the food supply that supports life
My judgments or laws — tied here to the justice sins

steps.whatToRemember: Corrupt judging and ביטול תורה bring war, plague, and famine. ברית means Torah, and 'rejecting My judgments' points to the justice sins.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'When I break for you the staff of bread,'
ten women will bake, etc.'
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues: 'they will return your bread by weight, and you will eat and not be satisfied.'

phrases.english: And it is written: 'Because, and precisely because, they rejected My judgments.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proofs for step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Famine and bread by weight come because of corrupt justice

steps.title: False oaths and desecration bring wild beasts and empty roads
steps.stepSummary: A new section. Four sins (שבועת שוא, שבועת שקר, חילול השם, חילול שבת) bring wild animals, loss of livestock, a shrinking population, and deserted roads.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the sin of a vain oath, a false oath, desecrating God's Name, and desecrating שבת: wild beasts increase, domestic animals are wiped out, people decrease in number, and the roads become desolate.
steps.whatsHappening: A new sin-and-punishment pair is stated. The proofs follow in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These four sins share a theme of treating holy things lightly: God's Name and שבת. The punishment is a land overrun by wild beasts, so cattle die, people grow few, and travel stops.

keyTerms.meaning: A vain oath — swearing to something obviously true or impossible
A false oath — swearing to a lie

phrases.english: Because of the sin of a vain oath and a false oath,
and desecrating God's Name, and desecrating Shabbat —
wild beasts increase, and domestic animals are wiped out,
and people decrease, and the roads become desolate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new set of sins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vain and false oaths, חילול השם, and חילול שבת bring wild beasts, loss of cattle, fewer people, and desolate roads.

steps.title: Reading 'these' as 'an oath' to link oaths to wild beasts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rereads 'באלה' (these) as 'באלה' (an oath). It then cites the nearby פסוק that promises wild beasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And if through these you will not be corrected for Me...' Do not read באלה ('these'); rather, read באלה ('an oath'). And it is written: 'I will send the wild beast of the field among you...'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves that vain oaths bring wild beasts. It uses an אל תקרי reading to find oaths hinted in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spelled without vowels, the same letters can be read 'these' or 'an oath'. Reading it as 'oath' makes the פסוק say 'if you are not corrected because of oaths'. The nearby curse of wild beasts then fits the ברייתא's list exactly: children taken, cattle destroyed, people few, roads desolate.

keyTerms.meaning: The beast of the field — wild animals

phrases.english: As it is said: 'And if through these you will not be corrected for Me' —
Do not read 'through these,' but rather 'through an oath.'

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וְהִשְׁלַחְתִּי בָכֶם אֶת חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: And it is written: 'And I will send among you the beast of the field, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first part of step 6, the oaths.
steps.raayaObject: Oaths bring wild beasts and desolation

steps.title: Linking all forms of desecration through the word חילול
steps.stepSummary: The word חילול appears for a false oath, for God's Name, and for שבת. A גזירה שוה extends the false-oath punishment to חילול השם and חילול שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written about a false oath: 'Do not swear falsely by My Name, and so desecrate the Name of your God.' And about desecrating God's Name it is written: 'Do not desecrate My holy Name.' And about desecrating שבת it is written: 'Those who desecrate it shall surely die.' And we learn חילול from חילול of a false oath.
steps.whatsHappening: So far only oaths were tied to wild beasts. This step uses a shared word to include the other two sins in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The false-oath פסוק uses the word חילול. The same word appears for God's Name and for שבת. Through a גזירה שוה, both of those sins receive the same punishment as a false oath: wild beasts and desolation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he derives' — learning one law from another
Desecration — the shared word that links the cases
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two places

steps.whatToRemember: Oaths, חילול השם, and חילול שבת all bring wild beasts and desolation. Oaths are proven by אל תקרי, and the other two through the shared word חילול.

phrases.english: And it is written regarding a false oath:
'And you shall not swear by My Name falsely,'
'and so desecrate the Name of your God.'
And regarding desecrating God's Name it is written:
'And you shall not desecrate My holy Name.'
And regarding desecrating Shabbat it is written: 'Those who desecrate it shall surely be put to death.'
And he derives 'desecration' from 'desecration' of a false oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the oath proof to cover the rest of step 6's list.
steps.raayaObject: חילול השם and חילול שבת share the false-oath punishment
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה from the word חילול in Leviticus 19:12, 22:32, and Exodus 31:14

steps.title: Bloodshed destroys the Temple and drives away the Divine Presence
steps.stepSummary: A new section. Because of שפיכות דמים, the בית המקדש is destroyed and the שכינה leaves Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the sin of bloodshed, the Temple is destroyed, and the Divine Presence departs from Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states a new sin and its punishment. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This punishment is different from the earlier ones. Instead of famine or wild beasts, the closeness between God and Israel itself is lost: the בית המקדש falls and the שכינה departs.

phrases.english: Because of the sin of bloodshed,
the Temple is destroyed,
and the Divine Presence departs from Israel,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new sin and punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bloodshed causes the destruction of the בית המקדש and the departure of the שכינה.

steps.title: If you defile the land, you will not live there and I will not dwell there
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק warns not to defile the land with blood. The ברייתא reads the reverse: if you do defile it, you will not live there and God will not dwell there.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Do not pollute... and do not defile the land in which you live, in whose midst I dwell.' This implies: if you defile it, you will not live in it, and I will not dwell in its midst.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves the bloodshed punishment. It infers the opposite of the פסוק's promise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק, which speaks about blood polluting the land, ties two things to a pure land: Israel living there and God dwelling there. So if the land is defiled by blood, both are lost. Losing the land matches the חורבן, and God not dwelling there matches the שכינה departing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This implies' — introduces an inference from the opposite case

steps.whatToRemember: Bloodshed defiles the land, which leads to exile and the loss of the שכינה. This is drawn as the reverse of the promise in במדבר 35:34.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is a central source for understanding חורבן and גלות as the result of the people's sins, especially שפיכות דמים.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'And you shall not pollute, etc.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:33. The words left out say that blood pollutes the land.

phrases.english: 'And you shall not defile the land'
'in which you dwell,'
'in whose midst I dwell.'
This implies: if you defile it —

phrases.aramaic: אֵינְכֶם יוֹשְׁבִים בָּהּ, וְאֵינִי שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹכָהּ.
phrases.english: you will not dwell in it, and I will not dwell in its midst.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the rule from step 9.
steps.raayaObject: Bloodshed leads to חורבן and the departure of the שכינה
steps.raayaSupportSource: Numbers 35:33–34, read by inferring the opposite

steps.title: Three sins that bring exile
steps.stepSummary: Because of גילוי עריות, עבודה זרה, and neglecting שמיטה and יובל, גלות comes. Israel is driven out and others take their place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the sin of forbidden relations, idol worship, and not keeping the שמיטה and יובל years, exile comes to the world. The people are exiled, and others come and live in their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new item in its list of sins and punishments. This time three sins together bring גלות (exile).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier punishments were wild animals, deserted roads, and the loss of the בית המקדש. Here the punishment goes further: the people lose the land itself, and strangers move into it. The next three steps prove each of the three sins from its own פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year, when the land must rest
The fiftieth year, also a year of rest for the land
Exile, being driven out of the land

phrases.english: Because of the sin of forbidden relations and idol worship
and neglecting the Shemitah and Yovel years
phrases.notes: Meaning they did not let the land rest in those years.

phrases.english: exile comes to the world,
and they are driven out,
and others come and settle in their place.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲוֹן גִּלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהַשְׁמָטַת שְׁמִיטִּין וְיוֹבְלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list of sins and punishments that began with earlier sections.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גילוי עריות, עבודה זרה, and neglecting שמיטה and יובל bring גלות, and others settle in Israel's place.

steps.title: Proof that forbidden relations bring exile
steps.stepSummary: פסוקים from the פרשת עריות say that the land is defiled and will 'vomit out' its people.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'For all these abominations the people of the land did…' And it is written: 'The land became impure, and I punished its sin upon it…' And it is written: 'So that the land will not vomit you out when you make it impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the first sin, גילוי עריות. It quotes the end of the פרשת עריות, which warns that the land will throw out people who defile it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These פסוקים come right after the list of forbidden relations. They call them 'abominations' that make the land impure. The image of the land 'vomiting out' its people is exactly the punishment in the מימרא: they are driven out and others replace them, as the nations before Israel were replaced.

keyTerms.meaning: It will vomit out (the land expelling its people)
And it is written, which introduces another פסוק

phrases.english: As it says: 'For all these abominations'
the people of the land did, etc.'
And it is written: 'And the land became impure'
and I punished its sin upon it, etc.'
And it is written: 'So that the land will not vomit you out'
when you make it impure.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי אֶת כׇּל הַתּוֹעֵבוֹת הָאֵל עָשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first of the three sins listed in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That גילוי עריות brings גלות and replacement by others.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא יח, כה–כח: the land is defiled and vomits out its inhabitants.

steps.title: Proof that idol worship brings exile
steps.stepSummary: The תוכחה connects idol worship with desolate sanctuaries and Israel being scattered among the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about idol worship it is written: 'I will throw your corpses…' And it is written: 'I will make your sanctuaries desolate…' 'And I will scatter you among the nations.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second sin, עבודה זרה. It quotes the curses in פרשת בחוקותי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק names idols ('your corpses upon your idols'), so it shows that these curses are about עבודה זרה. The same passage then speaks of desolation and of being scattered among the nations. That is the גלות promised in the מימרא.

phrases.english: And about idol worship it is written:
'I will throw your corpses, etc.'
phrases.notes: The verse continues 'upon the corpses of your idols', which ties it to עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'I will make your sanctuaries desolate, etc.'
'And I will scatter you among the nations.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second of the three sins listed in step 11.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כו, ל–לג: idols, desolate sanctuaries, scattering among the nations.

steps.title: Proof that neglecting שמיטה and יובל brings exile
steps.stepSummary: The land makes up its missed rest years while Israel is in its enemies' land.
steps.simpleTranslation: About שמיטה and יובל it is written: 'Then the land will make up its rest years all the days it lies desolate, while you are in your enemies' land…' And it is written: 'All the days it lies desolate it will rest.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the third sin, neglecting שמיטה and יובל. The פסוקים say the land will rest while the people are in exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is measure for measure. The people would not let the land rest, so they are removed, and the land gets back the rest it missed. The words 'you are in your enemies' land' show plainly that the punishment is גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: It will make up, repay (the missed rest years)

steps.whatToRemember: Three sins bring גלות: גילוי עריות (the land vomits out its people), עבודה זרה (sanctuaries made desolate, the people scattered), and neglecting שמיטה and יובל (the land takes back its missed rest while the people are in exile).

phrases.english: About Shemitah and Yovel years it is written:
'Then the land will make up its rest years'
all the days it lies desolate
while you are in your enemies' land, etc.'
And it is written: 'All the days it lies desolate it will rest.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the third and last sin listed in step 11, completing the section.
steps.raayaObject: That neglecting שמיטה and יובל brings גלות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כו, לד–לה: the land makes up its missed rest years while Israel is in its enemies' land.

steps.title: Vulgar speech brings troubles and unanswered cries
steps.stepSummary: Because of נבלות פה, troubles and harsh decrees increase, young people die, and orphans and widows cry out without being answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the sin of filthy speech, troubles multiply, harsh new decrees are made, the young men of Israel die, and orphans and widows cry out but are not answered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section with a new sin, נבלות פה (vulgar or filthy speech), and lists its punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Filthy speech might seem like a small sin, but the punishments are very harsh. They hit the whole nation: troubles, decrees, and the deaths of young people. The weakest people, orphans and widows, are hurt too, because their prayers go unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'enemies of Israel', a polite way of saying Israel itself

steps.confusionAlert: 'The young men of the enemies of Israel die' does NOT mean Israel's enemies are punished. The חז״ל did not want to say a curse directly about Israel, so they wrote 'enemies of Israel' in its place. It means the young men of Israel die.

phrases.english: Because of the sin of filthy speech, troubles multiply,
and harsh new decrees are made,
and the young men of 'the enemies of Israel' die,
phrases.notes: A polite way of referring to Israel itself.

phrases.english: orphans and widows cry out and are not answered,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new item in the list of sins and punishments, after the גלות section ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נבלות פה brings troubles, harsh decrees, the deaths of young people, and unanswered cries of orphans and widows.

steps.title: Proof from ישעיה for the punishment of vulgar speech
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in ישעיה says that because every mouth speaks vileness, God takes no joy in the young men and has no mercy on orphans and widows.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Therefore God will not rejoice over his young men, and He will not have mercy on his orphans and widows, because everyone is a flatterer and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks vileness. Even so, His anger has not turned back, and His hand is still stretched out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the punishments of נבלות פה from one פסוק in ישעיה. The verse lists the same punishments and gives the reason: 'every mouth speaks vileness'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the מימרא is in the פסוק. 'No joy in his young men' means the young men die. 'No mercy on orphans and widows' means their cries go unanswered. 'His hand is still stretched out' points to troubles and decrees that keep coming. The phrase 'every mouth speaks נבלה' shows that the cause is filthy speech.

keyTerms.meaning: A flatterer, a false or ungodly person
His hand is stretched out (more punishment is coming)

steps.whatToRemember: נבלות פה is treated as a very serious sin. Its punishment is national suffering, and even the prayers of orphans and widows go unanswered, as ישעיה ט says.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עַל כֵּן עַל בַּחוּרָיו לֹא יִשְׂמַח ה׳
phrases.english: As it says: 'Therefore God will not rejoice over his young men'
and on his orphans and widows He will not have mercy
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording, matching the פסוק exactly.

phrases.english: because everyone is a flatterer and an evildoer
and every mouth speaks vileness
even so, His anger has not turned back
and His hand is still stretched out.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עַל כֵּן עַל בַּחוּרָיו לֹא יִשְׂמַח ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the מימרא of step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That נבלות פה brings the deaths of young men, unanswered orphans and widows, and continuing troubles.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיה ט, טז: 'every mouth speaks vileness' is the cause, and the punishments follow.

steps.title: What does 'His hand is stretched out still' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the end of the פסוק in ישעיה quoted in the previous step.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'and His hand is stretched out still'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the last words of the ישעיה פסוק mean. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 quoted ישעיה about every mouth speaking vileness. That פסוק ends with 'ועוד ידו נטויה,' which sounds like an extra punishment beyond the ones already listed. The גמרא wants to know what that extra punishment is.

keyTerms.meaning: And His hand is stretched out still (more punishment is still coming)

phrases.english: What is meant by 'and His hand is stretched out still'?
phrases.notes: End of ישעיה 9:16, continuing the פסוק from step 16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the final phrase of the פסוק cited in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra punishment is meant by 'His hand is stretched out still'?

steps.title: Vulgar talk can reverse a good decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנן בר רבא explains that vulgar speech can turn a sealed decree of seventy good years into bad ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנן בר רבא said: Everyone knows why a bride enters the חופה. Even so, anyone who speaks vulgarly about it, even if a decree of seventy good years was sealed for him, they turn it to bad for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנן בר רבא answers the question. Even a sealed good decree is flipped to a bad one for someone who talks vulgarly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His example is a wedding. Everyone knows what happens there, so talking crudely about it reveals no secret, yet it is still a serious sin. The 'stretched out hand' means that even a good future that was already sealed can be reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes his mouth vile (speaks vulgarly)

steps.confusionAlert: The point is not that the bride's situation is a secret. It is the opposite: since everyone already knows, the crude speech adds nothing except vulgarity, and it is still punished.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanan bar Rava said:
Everyone knows about a bride
why she enters the wedding canopy.
Nevertheless, anyone who makes his mouth vile (about it),
even if they seal upon him a decree
of seventy years for good,
they turn it upon him for bad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'stretched out hand' means that even a sealed decree of seventy good years is reversed to bad.

steps.title: גיהנם is deepened for vulgar speakers
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that גיהנם is made deeper for one who speaks vulgarly, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said in the name of רב חסדא: Anyone who makes his mouth vile, they deepen גיהנם for him, as it says: 'A deep pit is the mouth of strange things.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching adds another punishment for נבלות פה: a deeper גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links 'mouth of strange (perverse) things' with a 'deep pit.' רב חסדא reads it to mean that vulgar speech digs a deeper pit in גיהנם for the speaker.

keyTerms.meaning: Gehinnom, the place of punishment after death

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbah bar Sheila said that Rav Chisda said:
Anyone who makes his mouth vile,
they deepen Gehinnom for him,
as it says: 'A deep pit is the mouth of strange things.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further punishment for נבלות פה beyond the reversed decree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גיהנם is deepened for one who speaks vulgarly.

steps.title: Even the silent listener is punished
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds that even someone who hears vulgar speech and stays silent falls into that pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Even one who hears and stays silent is punished, as it says: 'The one God is angry with will fall there.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the second half of the same פסוק to include the silent listener.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק spoke about the mouth that speaks. The second half says someone else 'will fall there.' רב נחמן בר יצחק learns that a listener who does not protest is also punished.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hears and stays silent
One whom ה׳ is angry with

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that responsibility for vulgar speech is not only on the speaker. Staying quiet while hearing it also counts.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Even one who hears and stays silent,
as it says: 'The one ה׳ is angry with will fall there.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אַף שׁוֹמֵעַ וְשׁוֹתֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב חסדא's teaching to include the listener, using the rest of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who hears vulgar speech and stays silent is also punished.

steps.title: Preparing oneself for sin brings wounds
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא teaches that someone who readies himself for sin will break out in wounds and bruises.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said: Anyone who prepares himself for sin, wounds and bruises come out on him, as it says: 'Wounds and bruises for one who prepares himself for evil.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related teaching about a different kind of sin: getting oneself ready to do wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תמרוק means polishing or preparing. רב אושעיא reads the פסוק to say that one who 'polishes' himself for evil gets wounds and bruises on his body.

keyTerms.meaning: One who polishes or prepares himself

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said:
Anyone who prepares himself for sin,
wounds and bruises break out on him,
as it says: 'Wounds and bruises for one who prepares himself for evil.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the punishment for vulgar speech to a similar teaching about preparing oneself for sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who prepares himself for sin is punished with wounds and bruises.

steps.title: He is also punished with הדרוקן
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא adds that such a person is also punished with הדרוקן, a swelling disease of the belly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but he is punished with הדרוקן, as it says: 'And blows to the inner chambers of the belly.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא continues his teaching. He uses the end of the same פסוק to add a second punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the פסוק speaks of blows inside the belly. That matches הדרוקן, a disease where the belly fills with fluid and swells.

keyTerms.meaning: A disease of swelling from fluid in the body (edema)
The inner chambers of the belly

phrases.english: And not only that, but he is punished with הדרוקן (edema),
as it says: 'And blows to the inner chambers of the belly.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב אושעיא's statement with an added punishment taken from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who prepares himself for sin is also punished with הדרוקן.

steps.title: הדרוקן is a sign of sin
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that הדרוקן is a sign that a person has sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: הדרוקן is a sign of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק sums up: הדרוקן can be a sign of sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said sin can cause הדרוקן. Now the direction is reversed: seeing הדרוקן can point to sin. This raises a worry that the next steps will address, because not every case of הדרוקן comes from sin.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
הדרוקן is a sign of sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: סִימָן לַעֲבֵירָה הִדְרוֹקָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the link between sin and הדרוקן into a sign that can be recognized.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הדרוקן is an indicator of sin.

steps.title: Three types of הדרוקן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three types of הדרוקן: from sin it is thick, from hunger it is swollen, and from witchcraft it is thin.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There are three kinds of הדרוקן. The one from sin is thick, the one from hunger is swollen, and the one from witchcraft is thin.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא shows that not all הדרוקן comes from sin. There are three kinds, and each looks different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This limits step 23. Only the thick kind points to sin. Swelling from hunger or from witchcraft has other causes and says nothing bad about the person.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude from step 23 that anyone with הדרוקן is a sinner. This ברייתא shows that only one of the three types comes from sin.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There are three types of הדרוקן:
the one from sin is thick,
and the one from hunger is swollen,
and the one from witchcraft is thin.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה מִינֵי הִדְרוֹקָן הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows step 23 by showing that הדרוקן has causes other than sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three kinds of הדרוקן, and only the thick kind comes from sin.

steps.title: שמואל הקטן's illness and cure
steps.stepSummary: שמואל הקטן got הדרוקן, asked God who could tell its cause, and was healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל הקטן fell ill with it. He said: Master of the World, who can cast lots (to tell what caused this)? He was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. A righteous man got הדרוקן and protested to God that no one could tell which kind it was, so people might suspect him of sin. He was then healed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל הקטן worried that people would think he had sinned, since no one can tell for sure which type he had. God healed him, which removed any suspicion and showed his illness was not from sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Who can cast lots (who can determine it)?

phrases.english: שמואל הקטן fell ill with it (הדרוקן).

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, מִי מֵפִיס?
phrases.english: He said: Master of the World, who can cast lots (to tell its cause)?
He was healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story of a righteous man with הדרוקן, building on the idea that its cause can vary.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A righteous person can get הדרוקן without sin, and שמואל הקטן was healed after his prayer.

steps.title: אביי's illness came from hunger
steps.stepSummary: אביי got הדרוקן, and רבא testified that it came from hunger because אביי starved himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי fell ill with it. רבא said: I know about נחמני (אביי) that he starves himself.
steps.whatsHappening: Another story. רבא defends אביי by explaining that his illness is the hunger type, not the sin type.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the ברייתא's second category. אביי ate very little, so his swelling was from hunger and says nothing about sin.

phrases.english: אביי fell ill with it.
רבא said:
I know about Nachmani (אביי)
that he starves himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story, applying the hunger category from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's הדרוקן was from hunger, not sin.

steps.title: Why would רבא get sick?
steps.stepSummary: רבא got הדרוקן. The גמרא asks how, since רבא himself warned that holding in one's needs kills more people than hunger, so he surely was careful about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא fell ill with it. But wasn't it רבא who said: More are killed by the pot (holding in one's needs) than are swollen from hunger?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רבא also got הדרוקן, then asks a challenge. רבא knew the danger of delaying going to the bathroom, so why would he get sick from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא did not starve himself, and we would not suspect him of sin. The one remaining cause was holding in his needs. But he himself taught how dangerous that is, so he would have been careful, which makes his illness hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Pot, referring to delaying relieving oneself

phrases.english: רבא fell ill with it.
But wasn't it רבא who said:
More are those killed by the pot (holding in one's needs)
than those swollen from hunger?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the explained cases of שמואל הקטן and אביי, raises a case that seems to have no innocent explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that רבא got הדרוקן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא did not starve himself, and he taught the danger of holding in his needs, so he would have avoided that cause. How then did he get sick, without suspecting him of sin?

steps.title: The Rabbis held רבא in place during his lecture
steps.stepSummary: רבא was different: the Rabbis forced him to stay while he taught, against his will, so he could not relieve himself in time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא is different, because the Rabbis forced him (to stay) during his lecture, against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא could not leave to relieve himself because the students kept him during his lecture. So his illness came from that, not from sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא knew the danger, but he was not in control. The Rabbis kept him teaching, so the cause was being held in place, with no sin and no carelessness on his part.
steps.whatToRemember: נבלות פה is punished very severely, even for the silent listener. Preparing oneself for sin can bring הדרוקן, but הדרוקן has several causes. The stories of שמואל הקטן, אביי, and רבא show that great people got it without sin, so one may not assume a sick person sinned.

phrases.english: רבא is different,
because the Rabbis forced him (to stay) during his lecture time,
against his will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא would have been careful, so his illness has no innocent explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was held in place against his will during his lecture, so his illness came from holding in his needs, not from sin.

steps.title: Four signs: each trouble points to a specific sin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four signs: הדרוקן is a sign of sin, ירקון of שנאת חנם, poverty of גסות הרוח, and אסכרה of לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There are four signs. A sign of sin is הדרוקן. A sign of hating people for no reason is ירקון (jaundice). A sign of arrogance is poverty. A sign of evil speech is אסכרה (a deadly throat disease).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that links four troubles to four sins. It continues the earlier topic of הדרוקן being caused by sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 already said one kind of הדרוקן comes from sin. This ברייתא widens the idea: several troubles can each point to a different sin. The last pair also fits 'measure for measure': לשון הרע is a sin of the mouth, and אסכרה is a disease of the throat.

keyTerms.meaning: Jaundice, which turns the skin yellow-green
Evil or harmful speech about others

steps.confusionAlert: Read 'סימן' as 'sign', not 'cause'. The ברייתא says these troubles can signal these sins. It does not say that everyone with jaundice or poverty is guilty of that sin. Step 24 already showed that הדרוקן can also come from hunger or witchcraft.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list sets up the next ברייתא. That ברייתא goes on to explain what sins bring אסכרה into the world.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: There are four signs:
A sign of sin is hidrokan (swelling disease),
phrases.notes: Connects to the ברייתא in step 24, which said one kind of הדרוקן comes from sin.

phrases.english: a sign of baseless hatred is jaundice,
a sign of arrogance is poverty,
phrases.notes: The arrogant person is brought low.

phrases.english: a sign of evil speech is askara (croup / throat disease).
phrases.notes: Measure for measure: a sin of the mouth is punished in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the earlier discussion of הדרוקן into a list of four illnesses or troubles, each linked to a specific sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four troubles are signs of four sins: הדרוקן of sin, ירקון of שנאת חנם, poverty of גסות הרוח, and אסכרה of לשון הרע.

steps.title: A new teaching begins about why אסכרה comes to the world
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא opens: 'אסכרה comes to the world...'. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: אסכרה comes to the world...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts a new ברייתא about what causes אסכרה, and the sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last ברייתא linked אסכרה to לשון הרע. This new ברייתא focuses on אסכרה alone. It will spell out which sins bring this disease into the world. Only the opening words appear here.

keyTerms.meaning: A deadly throat disease, often identified as croup or diphtheria

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Askara comes to the world
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud ('...as punishment for...').

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the last item in the list of four signs, אסכרה, and opens a new ברייתא devoted to its causes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of a ברייתא about the causes of אסכרה. The content is completed on the next amud.
